I thoroughly enjoyed this. Regarding the Barry mentioned, there's a popular brand of Irish tea called Barry's.

I am relying on memory for this, but the original justification for pouring the milk before the tea was to minimize the chance that hot tea poured into a delicate room-temperature teacup would shatter it. Room temperature in XIXth century Britain was about 68°F/ 20°C.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-578967

See aelanna's post in that thread. She also links to the tag guide.

Basically, a cognitohazard is a thing that affects your thoughts (or more) if you sense it an any way. In this case, by making people "[treat] 'him' like an irritating friend, or cantankerous older relative". The effects themselves are cognitohazardous. I guess :p

An infohazard is a thing that affects your thoughts/actions if you even know about it. But, being told about the dapper gentleman has no effect right?

A memetic affect is any mental effect that's contagious. The contagion itself is the meme.

These are not mutually exclusive. The cognitohazardous effect of a cognitohazard could also be memetic. But it doesn't seem to be in this case.

If it affects your actions, it's also a compulsion. But, in this case, is it:
1. You actually kinda think he's an irritating friend or relative, and the way you treat him is simply a result of that?
2. You treat him like that despite knowing it's not the appropriate way to react to him, because he's a total stranger.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks Shrike, I can definitely fix that. I was under the impression that cognitohazards were things like pictures that you see and then they affect you, which is why I assumed it was memetics instead. If someone else can confirm what Shrike says I'll go ahead and change it.

It's definitely one where you probably have to experienced the outright madness in real life, when it comes to people's tastes in how to make tea (I'm British). I've seen plenty of arguments first hand on the subject ranging from cheerful disagreements to people actually getting peed off and getting in a huff about it! Hence why it will probably resonate most with people from countries like the UK and New Zealand who drink a lot of tea with milk.

The serious tone came about as it was originally going to be a "normal" SCP, albeit a silly one. There are plenty in the database already such as the evil robot who is totally useless. Maybe it is more suitable as that. But a few people told me they thought it should be a Joke SCP instead so I went down that route for the rest of it. It's certainly not going to be to everyone's tastes as its quite dry humour.

If you think it should be resubmitted as a normal SCP with a bit of toning down on the bits you suggested, I'm all ears!

Thanks for the feedback.
